draft.title: Similarity and scale factors
card: Two shapes are similar if they have the same shape but may differ in size. Matching angles are equal, and matching sides are in the same ratio.
The scale factor is the ratio of matching sides: new length ÷ original length. Example: a side of 4 cm becomes 10 cm, so the scale factor is 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.
To find a missing side, multiply or divide by the scale factor. If the scale factor from small to large is 2.5, a 6 cm side on the small shape matches 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm on the large one.
Two triangles are similar if two pairs of angles are equal, or if all three pairs of sides are in the same ratio. Two equal angles are enough, as the third angle must then match too.
draft.remember: Similar shapes have equal angles and sides in a constant ratio, the scale factor.

a.q: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR. Side AB is 6 cm and matching side PQ is 15 cm. Side BC is 8 cm. How long is the matching side QR?
a.why: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5, so QR = 8 × 2.5 = 20 cm. Adding the difference of 9 cm to get 17 cm is tempting, but similar shapes scale by multiplying, not adding.
a.clue: Find the scale factor first, then multiply.

b.q: In triangle DEF, angle D is 50° and angle E is 70°. In triangle XYZ, angle X is 50° and angle Z is 60°. What can be said about the two triangles?
opts: They are similar, because two pairs of angles are equal
They are not similar, because the sides are not given
They are not similar, because only one angle matches
They are similar only if the side lengths are equal
b.why: Angle F = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°, and angle Y = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°. So all three angles match (D and X, E and Y, F and Z), and the triangles are similar. Side lengths are not needed, as equal angles are enough.
b.clue: Find the missing angle in each triangle first.

b.best: They are similar, because two pairs of angles are equal
